transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Robinson (Redwood SE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (ACME Head of Data Privacy), Marco Diaz (ACME CISO), Samantha Lee (ACME Legal), Ethan Wu (Platform Lead), Naomi Ortiz (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto): security review focusing on PHI/PII handling, encryption and retention; follow-ups agreed.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, and this is Leah on the se side, Omar's on if we need deeper infra questions.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, thanks. We're ACME Health pharma security and privacy team, so we'll jump right into questions. We have some must-haves for PHI handling and audits.
[00:22] Marco: Yeah, SOC two and ISO are the baseline for us, and then we need BYOK for anything that touches patient data.
[00:30] Jordan: Totally, understood. Leah, do you want to cover our compliance artifacts and deployment options first?
[00:35] Leah: Sure. Quick overview: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the hosted control plane and can provide the report under NDA. We also have an ISO 27001 certificate in our compliance pack. For customers requiring strict isolation, Redwood Private provides a customer-controlled control plane in a VPC or an on-prem option.
[00:52] Samantha: When you say "control plane in a VPC", is that fully customer-managed network-level isolation or is there still any Redwood-managed control plane elements?
[00:58] Leah: Good question. For Redwood Private we can deploy a private control plane that runs inside the customer's VPC. That means networking, subnets, and connectivity are under the customer's account; Redwood operates the software but the network is customer-controlled. For on-prem packages, there's an option where everything runs in your datacenter and we provide installation artifacts.
[01:15] Naomi: Do you support hybrid — e.g., model serving in our dc but control plane in Redwood?
[01:20] Leah: We do have hybrid patterns but for PHI we typically recommend either full private or dedicated reserved capacity where the data plane never leaves your network boundary. We'll follow up with architecture diagrams.
[01:30] Marco: What about key management? Does Redwood hold keys? Our policy is BYOK and HSM-backed keys.
[01:37] Leah: We support KMS integrations. For cloud deployments we integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault. For BYOK, you can bring your own key material and we can integrate with an HSM-backed KMS. In Private deployments you can configure the key endpoint inside the VPC and Redwood does not store the raw key material.
[01:56] Priya: Can you confirm encryption in transit and at rest, and whether logs contain any plaintext prompts or responses?
[02:03] Jordan: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit. At rest, model cache and artifacts are encrypted; customer content storage follows encryption-at-rest using the customer's KMS when BYOK is used. About logs: audit logs can be configured to scrub prompt content; by default we include metadata and request IDs, not prompt full text, but we need to confirm the exact retention and fields in the audit.
[02:30] Samantha: That default is important. We also need an explicit legal guarantee about "no training" on customer data for models. Can you provide language?
[02:38] Leah: Our policy is that Redwood does not train customer-provided prompts or content into open models. For hosted models we have a strict no-training-on-customer-data clause — I can paste the exact contract language in follow up. For shared models we don't use customer prompts to update model weights. For dedicated/private with on-prem, obviously you control model updates.
[02:55] Marco: Is that audited or just policy?
[02:57] Leah: It's in policy and part of our compliance pack; we can annotate the SOC2 scope that looks at data handling and model update processes. We'll surface the evidence in the SOC2 report and the internal security playbook.
[03:12] Ethan: About log retention and SIEM, what format are the audit logs? JSON? How long? Can we ship them to our Splunk/Datadog?
[03:20] Leah: Logs are JSON entries with timestamps, request IDs, model id, latency, token counts, and optional request metadata. Prompt/content fields are optional and can be redacted. Retention is configurable; hosted defaults to 30 days for full content but metadata is kept longer for billing, we can provide longer retention as an enterprise add-on or push to your SIEM via a push integration or S3 export.
[03:46] Naomi: Is the 30 days a hard limit? Our policy requires 90 days of access for logs.
[03:52] Jordan: We can configure a 90-day retention for logs as part of an enterprise contract; for PHI we usually recommend a private deployment and you can keep logs as long as you need in your own S3 bucket.
[04:05] Priya: On data residency — we are EU-based for patient records. Can you keep processing and storage inside the EU region?
[04:12] Leah: Yes, we have region routing and can pin processing to EU-only regions for hosted; for full data residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated in the EU region or Redwood Private inside your VPC in an EU datacenter.
[04:24] Marco: How do you handle data deletion / deletion at rest guarantees and legal holds? If a patient asks for right to be forgotten, what's the flow?
[04:31] Leah: We have data deletion APIs: you can submit deletion requests via the console or API; they remove records from customer content storage and purge caches. For legal holds we can suspend deletion for specified IDs and provide an audit trail. We'll send the exact retention/deletion SLA text.
[04:47] Samantha: We need to ensure deletion is deterministic — not just flagging.
[04:50] Leah: Understood — our deletion process performs physical deletion from content blobs; we will include the verification steps in the documentation. In some cloud providers S3 deletion still takes time due to object lifecycle, but we document the mechanisms and timelines.
[05:05] Marco: On RBAC and SSO, we use Okta & SCIM provisioning; do you support SCIM + SAML?
[05:11] Jordan: Yes. SSO via SAML / OIDC is supported; SCIM-based provisioning for groups & users is available for enterprise customers. We also support granular RBAC roles — e.g., auditor, infra, model-admin, billing.
[05:26] Ethan: Can we map roles to our internal groups and restrict token issuance by role?
[05:31] Leah: Absolutely; tokens can be issued with role-scoped permissions. We also support short-lived tokens and session revocation.
[05:38] Priya: About PII/PHI classification — do you have automatic redaction or tagging for sensitive fields before storage?
[05:45] Leah: We offer integrations with data-classification pipelines and can optionally redact PII using a pre-processing hook. For PHI we recommend doing the redaction or tokenization on your side prior to sending, but we can help design the pipeline.
[05:58] Marco: What's the mitigation if plaintext prompts accidentally get stored in logs? Is there an incident response flow?
[06:02] Jordan: We have an IR playbook: we notify affected parties, rotate any keys if needed, provide forensic logs, and root cause analysis. We'll include SOC2 incident handling sections in the follow-up pack.
[06:15] Samantha: Are you comfortable with security review questionnaires? We have a 200+ question vendor risk assessment.
[06:21] Jordan: Yes — our security team can ingest the VRA and we have a hosted VSA portal where we host the answers. We also have a compliance pack (SOC2, ISO 27001, penetration test summaries) we can share.
[06:31] Priya: Quick question — do you ever use customer data to fine-tune models or to improve your underlying models? We need an explicit "never fine-tune on customer content" for our policy.
[06:40] Leah: We will not fine-tune Redwood-managed models using customer content. Our commercial terms include a clause that customers' content isn't used to improve models. I will paste the contractual language in the follow up.
[06:50] Naomi: Do you maintain separate model weight stores for dedicated customers? And if a bug is fixed in the model, how are updates handled?
[06:57] Leah: For dedicated pools we can provide pinned model versions. You can choose to stay on a version or accept updates via controlled rollouts. For private on-prem, you manage upgrades.
[07:08] Marco: About audit logs again — can we get a streaming export to our SIEM in near real-time?
[07:13] Leah: Yes, we support push-to-S3 and webhooks; for higher security we can set up a direct log-forwarder to a collector inside your VPC and you can ingest into SIEM.
[07:23] Ethan: Any token-level cost visibility? Not security but ops related — how granular are logs for debugging?
[07:29] Jordan: We provide token-level counts and cost breakdowns in the console and via APIs; access to cost telemetry is role-gated.
[07:37] Marco: Regarding contractual indemnities — if there's a data breach caused by Redwood negligence, what's the typical approach?
[07:43] Samantha: We need to align limits and liabilities.
[07:45] Jordan: That's legal; we'll coordinate with our legal team and your counsel. Typically limits and cyber endorsements are negotiated for enterprise. We'll follow up.
[07:55] Priya: Are you SOC2 reports scoped to include model serving? We need the machine learning inference paths included.
[08:01] Leah: The SOC2 scope includes the hosted control plane and key production services; I'll confirm the exact services covered in the returned report. If necessary we can run an additional attestation for specific inference components.
[08:14] Marco: Can we get a pen test report or summary?
[08:17] Leah: We perform annual third-party pentests and can share the executive summary and remediation timeline under NDA.
[08:24] Samantha: For compliance evidence we also require retention of audit logs for 7 years for some records - is that possible?
[08:31] Jordan: For long-term retention we typically export to customer-managed storage; we don't promise to retain hosted content that long by default, but if you want us to store logs long-term in our system we can provide an enterprise plan. Best practice is E2 export to your own S3.
[08:49] Priya: A specific ask: can you provide signed attestation that Redwood will not use customer content for training or research and that prompts/responses will be purgeable upon request?
[08:58] Leah: Yes — we can provide contractual language and we have a standard attestation; we'll coordinate with legal to produce a signed statement.
[09:07] Jordan: We'll include that as an action item.
[09:14] Marco: How do you handle backups and snapshots — do they contain customer content? Are they encrypted and are keys customer-managed?
[09:22] Leah: Backups of customer content are encrypted; when BYOK is used, backups are encrypted with your KMS. Snapshots containing state might be encrypted with infrastructure keys in hosted mode; for Private and BYOK we can ensure customer-managed keys.
[09:39] Ethan: Network egress controls — can we restrict egress from servers to only internal endpoints?
[09:45] Leah: In private deployments yes, you control egress rules. For hosted we have egress controls but some services reach out for telemetry; we can minimize telemetry and route telemetry to customer endpoints under enterprise agreements.
[09:59] Naomi: Regarding SSO, do you support SCIM group sync for RBAC mapping?
[10:03] Jordan: Yes, SCIM group sync supported.
[10:06] Priya: Anything else we should expect in the compliance pack?
[10:09] Leah: You'll get SOC2 Type II under NDA, ISO 27001 cert, pen test executive summary, data processing addendum (DPA) with details on sub processors, data flow diagrams, and example contractual language for non-training and deletion.
[10:25] Samantha: We'll need the DPA before procurement can approve.
[10:28] Jordan: Understood; we'll prioritize that.
[10:33] Priya: On the technical side we may want a short bench test — can Redwood run a sample workload with synthetic PHI to validate that keys and VPC isolation behave as expected?
[10:42] Leah: Yes — we can run a controlled benchmark/poc in a dedicated pool or in your private environment. For PHI we recommend private or dedicated.
[10:53] Marco: Do you have data access logs that show which engineer/service accessed raw prompts? We need to know if anybody at Redwood can see plaintext content.
[11:02] Leah: Access is highly restricted; we have admin audit logs showing who accessed what. For hosted mode, standard support workflows may allow viewing of content if customer authorizes it; for PHI we strongly recommend private or dedicated so only customer-managed systems ever hold plaintext. We'll provide RBAC role definitions and support escalation flow.
[11:22] Jordan: Great. I'll summarize next steps in an email and attach the SOC2 and DPA.
[11:28] Priya: Thanks. Quick clarifying note: when you say "we don't train on customer data" — does that include embeddings and vector stores that we might request?
[11:37] Leah: Embeddings and customer vectors are treated as customer content; they are not used to train Redwood models. For managed index services we do not leak aggregated vectors into global model training. We can add contractual language.
[11:51] Naomi: Any caveats about telemetry — does telemetry include hashed prompt-level features?
[11:56] Leah: Telemetry can include token counts and patterns but not raw prompt text unless enabled. We'll provide the telemetry schema.
[12:07] Samantha: Ok — this is enough for the first pass. We'll wait for SOC2, DPA, KMS diagrams and the signed attestation on no-training.
[12:16] Jordan: Yep — action items and next steps on the shared doc. Thanks, everyone.
[12:20] Priya: Thanks.
[12:23] End meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: some names mis-typed by auto-transcript, occasional overlap. There are a few places where "KMS" transcribed as "K-M-S" and "SOC 2" as "SOC two".
